sources.title: Mem0 raises $24M to build the memory layer for AI (company announcement)
sources.summary: Mem0's own Series A post: $24M total (Seed led by Kindred, Series A led by Basis Set) plus adoption metrics and the AWS Agent SDK partnership. Best primary evidence of OSS-to-cloud conversion velocity in this category.
key_facts: Mem0 raised $24M total: Seed led by Kindred Ventures, Series A led by Basis Set Ventures (Oct 2025)
Other investors: Peak XV Partners, GitHub Fund, Y Combinator; angels incl. Scott Belsky, Dharmesh Shah, Datadog/Supabase/PostHog/W&B CEOs
Adoption: 'crossed 41,000 GitHub stars' and '14 million Python package downloads'
API calls grew from 35 million (Q1 2025) to 186 million (Q3 2025)
AWS selected Mem0 as 'exclusive memory provider for their new Agent SDK'
Native integrations in CrewAI, Flowise, Langflow; 'thousands of teams... Fortune 500 companies use us in production'
Post does not say how developers discovered the product or how funds will be used

sources.title: Mem0 raises $24M from YC, Peak XV and Basis Set to build the memory layer for AI apps
sources.summary: Press coverage of Mem0's $24M raise (Oct 28, 2025), confirming investor list and positioning as a horizontal memory layer sold to agent builders.
key_facts: TechCrunch dated Oct 28, 2025: Mem0 $24M combined seed + Series A
Series A led by Basis Set Ventures; participation from Peak XV, GitHub Fund, Y Combinator
Positioning: memory layer 'integrated with just three lines of code'

sources.title: Mem0 Raises $24M Series A to Build Memory Layer for AI Agents (press release)
sources.summary: Official press release listing strategic angel investors from infrastructure companies, a signal of the infra-founder channel Mem0 used for credibility.
key_facts: Strategic angels: CEOs of Datadog, Supabase, PostHog, Weights & Biases, ex-GitHub CEO, Scott Belsky, Dharmesh Shah
Claims 'thousands of teams, from startups to Fortune 500 companies' in production

sources.title: Mem0 Pricing
sources.summary: Mem0's cloud tiers (fetched Aug 2026): request-metered plans from free to $249/mo, with on-prem, audit logs and SSO gated to Enterprise. Shows the add-vs-retrieve metering model and where enterprise features sit.
key_facts: Hobby: free, 10,000 add requests/mo, 1,000 retrieval requests/mo, 1 project
Starter: $19/mo, 50,000 add + 5,000 retrieval requests/mo, 1 project
Pro: $249/mo, 500,000 add + 50,000 retrieval requests/mo, unlimited projects, graph memory, 'Dream (Memory Consolidation)', private Slack
Enterprise (custom): unlimited requests, on-prem deployment, audit logs, custom integrations & SSO, SLA support
Also offers 'usage-based pricing for teams whose traffic doesn't map cleanly to a fixed tier'

sources.title: Letta Pricing (Letta Code / Cloud)
sources.summary: Letta's pricing (letta.com/pricing now 301-redirects here, Aug 2026) is built around stateful agents as the billing unit, with seat-based team plans and an API plan per active agent. Notably no SOC2/on-prem/BYOC mentioned on the page.
key_facts: Free: $0, max 3 stateful agents, limited Letta Auto usage, BYOK
Pro: $20/mo, up to 20 stateful agents, Letta Auto weekly+monthly quota, PAYG overage
API plan: $20/mo base + $0.10 per active agent/mo + $0.00015/sec tool execution, PAYG LLM usage
Teams Pro: $20/seat/mo; Enterprise: custom, volume pricing, RBAC, SAML/OIDC SSO
No SOC2, on-prem or BYOC options mentioned on pricing page as of Aug 2026
letta.com/pricing redirects to docs.letta.com/letta-code/pricing: Letta Code is now the front door

sources.title: Zep Pricing
sources.summary: Zep's credit-metered cloud pricing (fetched Aug 2026) with annual-billed Flex tiers and an Enterprise tier that explicitly lists SOC 2 Type II, HIPAA BAA, BYOC and EU DPA, the most compliance-forward packaging among the memory vendors.
key_facts: Free: 10,000 credits/mo, 2 projects, 1 Memory MCP Server seat
Flex: $1,250/yr (~$104/mo), 50,000 credits/mo then $25 per 10,000 credits, 600 req/min, 5 projects
Flex Plus: $3,750/yr (~$312/mo), 200,000 credits/mo then $75 per 40,000, 1,000 req/min, 10 projects
Credit unit: 'Episodes up to 350 bytes use 1 credit'; storage and retrieval unmetered
Enterprise: SOC 2 Type II, HIPAA BAA, 1-year audit/API logs, Cloud / Cloud+BYOK / BYOC (your VPC), DPA for EU
MCP Server seats are a packaging dimension (1 / 5 / 15 / custom)

sources.title: Supermemory Pricing
sources.summary: Supermemory's pricing (fetched Aug 2026) bundles usage credits with connectors (Drive, Notion, Gmail, GitHub) and plugins (Claude Code, OpenClaw, Hermes), and meters memory per 1K tokens; SOC2/HIPAA and self-hosting start at the $399 Scale tier.
key_facts: Free: $0 with ~$5/mo usage credits, Supermemory MCP, Hermes plugin
Pro $19/mo (~$20 credits), Max $100/mo (~$130 credits), Scale $399/mo (~$600 credits, up to 10 teammates)
Usage rates: memory $0.005 per 1K tokens ($0.010 rich), SuperRAG $0.001 per 1K tokens, search $0.005 per 1K queries
Scale/Enterprise: SOC 2, HIPAA BAA, self-hosted option, 'air-gapped self-hosting'
Enterprise includes 'Forward Deployed engineer' and committed-spend pricing
Connectors (Gmail, Granola, GitHub, S3, web crawler) used as tier differentiators

Led by Susa Ventures with Browder Capital and SF1.vc (per search snippet)
Angels: Jeff Dean (Google), Dane Knecht (Cloudflare CTO), Logan Kilpatrick (DeepMind), David Cramer (Sentry)

sources.title: Show HN: Mem0 - open-source Memory Layer for AI apps
sources.summary: Mem0's original Show HN (Sept 4, 2024): 201 points, 61 comments. Critiques foreshadow today's buyer objections: OSS commitment, PII handling via prompts, relevancy scoring, memory bloat, over-engineering.
key_facts: 201 points, 61 comments, posted Sept 4, 2024
Critique: 'will you support the open source version as a first class citizen for the long term?'
Critique on PII: 'Do you just rely on the LLM to follow instructions perfectly?'
Critique: demo showed 9/10 relevancy for '100% duplication' of user input
Critique: 'memory bloat' and handling 'outdated or irrelevant memories over time'; 'Looks very over engineered'
Praise: 'solves a real problem'; hybrid datastore 'smart'; competitors cited: ChatGPT memory, Claude prompt caching

sources.title: Ask HN: Mem0 stores memories, but doesn't learn user patterns
sources.summary: Feb 2026 thread from a YC W23 founder: Mem0/Letta solve fact storage plus semantic search but not implicit preference learning from user corrections; others report 'hitting same wall'. Small thread but a clear unmet-need signal.
key_facts: 9 points, 7 comments, ~Feb 2026; poster is YC W23 founder building agents for engineering labs
Complaint: Mem0 = 'key-value memory with semantic search', fails at learning patterns like repeated threshold edits 85%->80%
Poster built internal API: structured events -> LLM -> confidence-weighted preference profile
Commenter: 'user corrections are the highest-signal data'; 'chat history mining' sector underdeveloped
Another startup (Slice) reports 'hitting same wall' and asks for docs

sources.title: Show HN: Mnemora - Serverless memory DB for AI agents (no LLM in your CRUD path)
sources.summary: 2026 Show HN that positions against Mem0/Zep/Letta on latency and token cost: those products route every write through an LLM; Mnemora does direct DB CRUD. Shows the 'LLM-in-the-write-path' objection has become a wedge for new entrants.
key_facts: Pitch: addresses 'latency and token cost issues of solutions like Mem0, Zep, and Letta'
Mechanism: direct database CRUD instead of routing data through an LLM on every operation

sources.title: Show HN: Mnemosyne - Cognitive memory OS for AI agents (zero LLM calls)
sources.summary: Another 2026 entrant differentiating on zero LLM calls: a deterministic 12-step pipeline with local embeddings instead of LLM extraction, again targeting cost/latency/determinism complaints about incumbents.
key_facts: Differentiator: deterministic 12-step pipeline with local embeddings, 'zero LLM calls'
Explicitly contrasts with systems that send text to an LLM for extraction

sources.title: Show HN: SuperLocalMemory - AI memory that stays on your machine, forever free
sources.summary: 2026 local-first alternative explicitly pitched against cloud memory (Mem0) for Claude users: privacy and 'forever free' as the wedge, signaling a segment that rejects hosted memory.
key_facts: Pitch: local memory for Claude stored on your machine 'instead of requiring cloud storage like Mem0'
Wedge: privacy + free, aimed at coding-agent users

sources.summary: Zep's 2023 launch thread (foundational): started as an open-source long-term memory store with summarization, vector search and SDKs before evolving into Graphiti plus a compliance-heavy cloud.
key_facts: 2023 launch features: long-term memory persistence, auto-summarization, vector search, token counting, Python + JS SDKs
Trajectory: OSS memory store (2023) -> Graphiti temporal graph + SOC2/HIPAA cloud (2026)

notes: Searched (8 of 12 WebSearch before the session-wide search budget hit 200/200, which blocked the last 4 queries): Mem0 funding/adoption; Letta pricing/funding; Zep pricing/SOC2; Supermemory funding/pricing; HN Show HN memory threads; context/memory engineer job postings; framework integration channels (LangGraph/CrewAI/Vercel/MCP); customer case studies. Fetched (8 of 8): mem0.ai/pricing, getzep.com/pricing, supermemory.ai/pricing, docs.letta.com/letta-code/pricing (letta.com/pricing 301s there), HN Mem0 Show HN (201 pts), HN Ask HN Mem0 user-patterns thread, mem0.ai/series-a. COULD NOT COVER (caps hit before these ran): founder interviews on first customers (Latent Space/YC talks); LangSmith, Pinecone and Chroma Cloud pricing pages; AWS AgentCore Memory / OpenAI memory incumbent moves and PII-unlearning governance requirements; funding for Cognee/Hindsight/Honcho/Graphlit; named enterprise case studies (search results were comparison articles, none with first-party customer stories); Discord sizes; npm download counts. Attribution caveats: WebSearch returns aggregated snippets, so facts tagged 'per search snippet' (Letta $10M Felicis seed, Letta Code 42.5% Terminal-Bench, Graphiti 28K stars, Supermemory 26.8K stars, Susa-led seed) are attributed to the most likely source page but were not fetched directly. Supermemory seed amount conflicts: $3M (company blog) vs $2.6M (press/LinkedIn). Value Add VC's '65% of failures = context drift' has no visible primary source. Recurring buyer-need themes across sources: (1) LLM-in-the-write-path latency/token cost is the #1 wedge for 2026 entrants; (2) compliance (SOC2/HIPAA/BYOC) is a tier gate and Zep's core positioning; (3) OSS-first then hosted cloud is the universal GTM, with framework-integration catalogs (Mem0: 25+, AWS exclusive) as the distribution moat; (4) unmet need: implicit preference learning from user corrections, not just fact storage; (5) Letta's pivot toward Letta Code suggests pure memory-infra is hard to monetize standalone.
